title: Speed Run: The Experimental Architect's Gauntlet

questions.question: Speed Check: In a 2 x 3 x 2 factorial design, how many total experimental conditions exist?
questions.explanation: Multiplying the factor levels: 2 x 3 x 2 = 12 unique experimental treatment cells.

questions.question: Speed Check: True or False — Random assignment to conditions is possible in a quasi-experimental design.

options.text: False (quasi-experiments by definition lack random assignment)

questions.explanation: The core defining feature of a quasi-experiment is the absence of random assignment.

questions.question: Speed Check: What does an inverted U-curve relationship (like the Yerkes-Dodson Law) produce on a Pearson correlation coefficient?

options.text: r ≈ 0.00 (because Pearson's r evaluates only linear relationships)

questions.explanation: Because the opposing halves of an inverted U cancel out mathematically in a linear formula, Pearson's r registers near zero.

questions.question: Speed Check: Which measurement scale possesses equal numeric intervals AND an absolute, non-arbitrary true zero point?
questions.explanation: Ratio scales feature both equal intervals and an absolute true zero point where the measured property is completely absent.

questions.question: Speed Check: What is the minimum standard threshold for acceptable internal consistency reliability (Cronbach's alpha)?
questions.explanation: In psychological research, Cronbach's alpha should generally equal or exceed 0.70 to establish adequate internal consistency.

questions.question: Speed Check: If cell lines on a factorial line plot cross each other in a bold 'X', what type of effect is occurring?
questions.explanation: Intersecting cell lines on a factorial graph represent a crossover interaction.

questions.question: Speed Check: When is an ABAB reversal single-case design ethically prohibited?

options.text: When withdrawing treatment would lead to severe, life-threatening harm (e.g., self-injury)
When the baseline phase lasts longer than 3 days
When testing in a school classroom

questions.explanation: Withdrawing an effective treatment that prevents dangerous or self-injurious behavior violates human subjects protection principles.
